name: CIRTS (CRISPR–Cas-Inspired RNA Targeting System)
therapeuticGoalDescription: Recruit programmable RNA effectors to specific transcripts for RNA editing, degradation, translation control, or imaging without altering genomic DNA.
molecularDefect: Pathogenic RNA sequence requiring programmable editing or transcript-specific regulation.
diseaseMechanism: A guide RNA directs the CIRTS effector complex to the target RNA. The effector domain (e.g., ADAR deaminase) performs site-specific RNA editing or other RNA modifications.
suitableVariantTypes: Single-nucleotide variants amenable to A→I editing; selected missense variants; nonsense variants; splice-site variants; RNA-level regulatory defects.
typicalDiseases: Experimental proof-of-concept only; proposed for monogenic neurological, metabolic, and retinal disorders. No disease-specific clinical program established.
rnaTargetRegion: Exonic or splice-site regions complementary to the guide RNA.
transcriptRequirement: Accessible target RNA with an appropriate guide-binding region.
typicalLength: Guide RNA length varies depending on construct design.
designRules: Design a guide RNA complementary to the target transcript; choose an appropriate effector domain (e.g., ADAR); experimentally validate editing efficiency and specificity.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Accessible RNA target region; excessive secondary structure may reduce guide binding.
offTargetConsiderations: Guide RNA cross-reactivity; bystander editing; unintended RNA binding; effector-specific off-target activity.
advantages: Modular platform; programmable; supports multiple RNA functions (editing, degradation, localization, imaging); no genomic DNA modification.
limitations: Early-stage technology; requires engineered protein delivery; no clinical trials; delivery remains challenging.

references.paper: Rauch S. et al. Programmable RNA-Guided RNA Effector Proteins Built from Human Parts. Cell (2019)
references.usedFor: Original description of the CIRTS platform.
Improved programmable RNA editing and targeting.

references.usedFor: Comparison of CIRTS, LEAPER, CRISPR-Cas13, and engineered ADAR systems.
